title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

reading.body:
This is insider misuse of a working system rather than a system that malfunctioned. The license-plate readers did what they were built to do, and the failure sat at the query layer, where a person with legitimate credentials entered plates and checked locations for a purpose the deployment was never meant to serve. The same access that supports police work also supports stalking, and nothing in the account suggests the tool distinguished between the two.

Catching it would have taken review of the query log rather than the camera feed. Repeated lookups tied to one person over months, with no corresponding case, is the pattern an audit would surface, and the order's finding that the chief also followed the couple in a police vehicle points to conduct that existed outside the system as well. The account does not say whether any such review occurred, or whether the misuse was found through an audit, a complaint, or another route.

What is not established is the exact number of lookups: the headline reports 164 and the summary of the certification order reports 228, and the two figures are not reconciled here. The certification order is an administrative finding, and whether any criminal charge followed is not stated.

reports.title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

summary: According to a Kansas certification order, Sedgwick, Kansas, Police Chief Lee Nygaard used Flock Safety license-plate readers 228 times from June to October 2023 to check the whereabouts of his ex-girlfriend and her new boyfriend. The order said he also followed them in a police vehicle and admitted jealousy influenced his conduct. Nygaard resigned in October 2023 and later lost his police certification.
